cells.name: Kid — wants: Find the dog that didn't come home.

cells.name: Animate teacup waiter — hops table to table on a saucer for legs, always resetting a spilled tray
Mushroom-capped gardener — squat body, wide round cap for a head, tends the sugar-beet patch
Walking alarm-clock postman — ticking loudly, always three minutes early
Candy-corn shopkeeper — triangular striped body, sells sweets that double as currency
Plaid-vested fox tailor — measures customers with a tape that never quite tells the truth
Round-bellied frog innkeeper — croaks out the nightly specials
Animate broom sweeper — no visible face, still somehow deeply expressive
Acorn-capped squirrel banker — counts coins faster than anyone can watch
Puffball cloud-person mail sorter — drifts a few inches off the ground, always
Piano-key zebra musician — stripes double as sheet music somehow
Jelly-bean-jar merchant — body made of stacked jellybeans, restocks himself
Waddling duck constable — badge too big for his chest, takes the job very seriously
Star-shaped night-watchman — glows faintly, patrols after the park closes
Carnivorous flower-person florist — sells bouquets, watches the customers a beat too long
Animate umbrella doorman — opens for rain or trouble, whichever comes first
Beanstalk-vine gardener — grows a little taller every scene, never mentions it
Egg-shaped chef — cracks a hairline more each time he laughs, never actually breaks
Round hedgehog cobbler — quills double as extra hands for pinning leather
Bunny-eared candy-striper nurse — the park infirmary's only real professional
Animate wind-up-key vendor — sells the keys that wind up the wind-up soldiers
Sunflower-headed farmer — turns to face whichever direction the crowd's headed
Puppet-jointed marionette librarian — strings visible, moves like she doesn't notice them
Round raccoon pickpocket, comic not menacing — always gets caught, never minds
Chubby bee beekeeper — tends the hives that make the park's actual honey
Animate lollipop crossing-guard — stops traffic with a literal giant sucker sign
Owl-faced night librarian — reads by moonlight, never needs the lamp
Penguin-shaped ice-cream vendor — waddles the exact same route every single day
Animate pocket-watch clockmaker — every gear visible, ticks faintly when he talks
Cat-eared seamstress — sews costumes for every performer in the park
Turtle-shelled mailman — slow, reliable, never once late in living memory
Animate paintbrush portrait artist — bristles for fingers, always mid-stroke
Round marshmallow baker — a little too warm to the touch, sells s'mores
Firefly lamplighter — lights the park's lanterns at dusk with no ladder
Puffin-faced ferry operator — runs the little boat ride, sings off-key sea shanties
Animate top-hat, a magician's assistant — the hat does most of the actual talking
Chipmunk-cheeked snack vendor — cheeks somehow hold an entire tray of popcorn
Round dumpling dim-sum chef — steam constantly rising off his own head
Butterfly-winged face-painter — dusts glitter off her wings between customers
Gopher-toothed construction foreman — rebuilds the same ride every season
Animate scarecrow security guard — straw arms, surprisingly firm grip
Round pufferfish balloon-seller — puffs up when startled, still smiling
Fox-eared fortune-cookie vendor — every fortune is oddly, specifically true
Animate music-box dancer, off-duty — pirouettes even just walking to work
Badger-faced blacksmith — forges the park's ride parts by hand, old-school
Round spider seamstress — eight hands, finishes orders twice as fast as anyone
Animate paper-lantern lamplighter's apprentice — glows a little dimmer, still learning
Squirrel-tailed accountant — counts the park's take twice, trusts no one, not even himself
Frog-throated town crier — announces every parade a little too loudly
Animate sock-puppet street performer — no visible strings, unsettlingly lifelike
Round hedgehog paperboy — quills hold the rolled-up newspapers
Beetle-shelled roller-rink DJ — shell doubles as a speaker somehow
Animate gingerbread baker's apprentice — smells faintly of cinnamon at all times
Bat-winged night-shift janitor — cleans the park after the lights go down
Round otter lifeguard — the water-ride's actual only qualified rescuer
Animate kite street-vendor — the kites tug at him like they want to fly off on their own
Chipmunk twins running the popcorn stand — synchronized, mildly unnerving
Round frog-faced ticket-taker — croaks out 'one, please' all day long
Animate wind-chime musician — sways gently even indoors
Fox-tailed reformed pickpocket, now security — still has the fastest hands in the park
Round snail mail-cart pusher — slow, but nothing ever gets lost
Human parade coordinator, dark-skinned — one of the few flesh-and-blood staff, keeps the too-cheerful schedule running
Elderly human ride mechanic — been fixing rides here since before most of the toons remember
Human ticket-booth kid, freckled — new hire, still adjusting to coworkers who are literally alive teacups
Human night-shift security guard — the toons handle most of it, he mostly just watches
Multi-ethnic human tour guide — explains the park to visitors who don't realize how much of it is actually alive
Elderly human food vendor — one of the last humans who still cooks by hand instead of somehow being made of the food itself
Human janitor — cleans up glitter and confetti that never seems to actually run out
Human maintenance crew lead, dark-skinned — the only one who goes near the rides when they're 'resting'
Human first-aid station nurse — treats human guests; the toon staff mostly can't be hurt the same way
Human retired performer — used to be in the park's old human-only sideshow, stayed on as groundskeeper
Human accountant — audits a park whose currency is sometimes literal candy
Human new hire, still visibly shaken — first week, still hasn't adjusted to a coworker being a sentient teapot
Human longtime resident — grew up beside the park, one of a handful of humans who actually live inside its boundary

cells.name: Land-worker (Dragonborn)
cells.cue: Tied to the land and its seasons; the base everyone eats from.

cells.name: Wild-provider (Dwarf)
cells.cue: Reads the wild and brings in what the settled can't.

cells.name: Hauler (Elf)
cells.cue: Moves the heavy things; sees everything, is asked nothing.

cells.name: Delver (Gnome)
cells.cue: Works the dark and the tight places; patient underground.

cells.name: Servant (Goliath)
cells.cue: Invisible to the powerful, and so hears every secret.

cells.name: Destitute (Halfling)
cells.cue: Has nothing, so knows the streets better than anyone.

cells.name: Maker (Human)
cells.cue: Their tools carry their whole history.

cells.name: Metalworker (Orc)
cells.cue: Calloused hands; deals in practical defense.

cells.name: Feeder (Tiefling)
cells.cue: Up before dawn; holds the neighborhood's gossip.

cells.name: Builder (Dragonborn)
cells.cue: Reads every structure out of habit; knows what's load-bearing.

cells.name: Clothier (Dwarf)
cells.cue: Notices the cut and quality of everyone's clothes.

cells.name: Outfitter (Elf)
cells.cue: Keeps the means of travel and trade running; eyes on the weather.

cells.name: Trader (Gnome)
cells.cue: Information-rich, truth-poor.

cells.name: Host (Goliath)
cells.cue: Controls the space, not the people in it.

cells.name: Remedy-maker (Halfling)
cells.cue: Smells of bitterroot; knows what heals and what doesn't.

cells.name: Healer (Human)
cells.cue: Trusted, and overburdened by it.

cells.name: Rite-keeper (Orc)
cells.cue: Maintains the ritual, not the doctrine.

cells.name: Performer (Tiefling)
cells.cue: Craves the attention; hides the true feeling under it.

cells.name: Enforcer (Dragonborn)
cells.cue: Authority-adjacent, with limited real power.

cells.name: Hired-blade (Dwarf)
cells.cue: Loyalty bought with coin, and cynical about it.

cells.name: Road-guard (Elf)
cells.cue: Wary of the road; values a good pair of boots.

cells.name: Outlaw (Gnome)
cells.cue: Desperate or cruel; lives outside the law.

cells.name: Smuggler (Goliath)
cells.cue: Hides the cargo; speaks only in euphemism.

cells.name: Thief (Halfling)
cells.cue: Eyes every coin-pouch; avoids every eye.

cells.name: Hidden-fanatic (Human)
cells.cue: Fanatical devotion behind a mundane face.

cells.name: Recruiter (Orc)
cells.cue: Charisma aimed at the desperate; sells belonging.

cells.name: Outsider (Tiefling)
cells.cue: Chose to stay here; the reasons stay unclear.

cells.name: Recluse (Dragonborn)
cells.cue: Known of, rarely seen.

cells.name: Stand-in (Dwarf)
cells.cue: Filling in for someone absent; borrowed authority.

cells.name: Unofficial-power (Elf)
cells.cue: Power without a title.

cells.name: Misfit (Gnome)
cells.cue: Unqualified, unwilling, or both — and in the role anyway.

cells.name: Pampered-elite (Goliath)
cells.cue: Wealthy, bored, insulated from real consequence.

cells.name: Magnate (Halfling)
cells.cue: Sees every interaction as a transaction.

cells.name: Secret-scholar (Human)
cells.cue: Hoards the secret knowledge; sees others as material.

cells.name: Cipher (Orc)
cells.cue: Their very presence is the notable thing.

cells.name: Dwarven forge-master — three generations of the same smithy, soot in every crease
Elven archivist — keeper of a library older than the town around it
Halfling innkeeper — knows every traveler's business before they've unpacked
Orcish caravan guard — hired muscle with a reputation for actually caring about the cargo
Tiefling fortune-teller — half the town swears by her, half crosses the street
Gnomish tinkerer — clockwork contraptions that mostly work
Goliath quarry foreman — the only one strong enough to reset a slipped cart alone
Dragonborn temple guard — devout, literal-minded, takes the oath seriously
Human miller — dust-covered, counts every sack twice
Dwarven brewer — the tavern's actual reason for existing
Elven fletcher — every arrow leaves her stall true
Halfling farmer, dark-skinned — tends the best soil in the valley
Orcish healer — gentle hands, a reputation people are slow to trust
Tiefling blacksmith's apprentice — still learning, already better than most journeymen

Domestic animal — A single goose from the flock — loud, territorial, first to mark a stranger.
Domestic animal — A single sheep from the herd — moves with the others, and its lone reluctance to follow is the tell.
Domestic animal — Bird kept close (a single hawk) — carries, watches, and remembers a face.
Domestic animal — Vermin-catcher (a single ferret) — goes gladly where people won't.
Domestic animal — Old animal — past its working years, half-blind, and still the first to growl at the wrong thing.
Domestic animal — Half-tamed wild thing — comes to the window, never the hand; trusts one child and no one else.
Domestic animal — The realm-beast (a war-mule, unfazed by artillery, carries what the quartermaster can't)
Domestic animal — The town's own animal — the one everyone knows by name; its fate is the town's mood made visible.
Domestic animal — A single rabbit — twitchy, kept for the table or kept as a pet, never sure which.
Domestic animal — A single pony — smaller and calmer than the war-mule, a child's first mount.
Domestic animal — A single duck — waddling, unbothered, first to notice a stranger at the water's edge.
Domestic animal — A single turkey — puffed up and loud, more guard animal than anyone admits.
Domestic animal — A single caged songbird — kept for the sound of it, restless behind the wire.
Domestic animal — A single turtle — slow-kept yard animal, older than most of the household.
Domestic animal — A single pig — smarter than it's given credit for, rooting at the fence line.
Domestic animal — A single goat — headstrong, climbs what it shouldn't, eats what it shouldn't.
Domestic animal — A single donkey — stubborn, sure-footed, outlives every horse on the property.
Domestic animal — A single peacock — kept for show, screams like something's wrong when nothing is.
Domestic animal — A single hunting hound — lean, nose-down, bred for the chase and bored without it.
Domestic animal — A single kitten — too young to have earned the barn cat's independence yet.
Domestic animal — A single caged ferret-kit — young, hyperactive, still learning the vermin-catcher's trade.
Kept Ornamental Koi
cells.cue: Officers' garden-pond fish, kept for calm color amid the noise, unfazed by distant guns.

cells.name: Water Buffalo
cells.cue: Broad, mud-caked draft beast hauling supply carts through the worst ground.

cells.name: Camel
cells.cue: Long-legged pack animal for the dry-front supply lines, unbothered by dust or noise.

cells.name: Llama
cells.cue: Sure-footed high-ground pack animal, spits when crowded, carries more than it looks like it should.

cells.name: Alpaca
cells.cue: Fleece-heavy pack animal kept partly for wool, partly for the wool's camouflage-grey shade.

cells.name: Yak
cells.cue: Shaggy cold-front draft beast, hauls guns and gear where nothing wheeled can go.

cells.name: Reindeer
cells.cue: Antlered northern-front sled and pack animal, moves silent over snow no truck could cross.

cells.name: Draft Zebu
cells.cue: Hump-backed plow-ox variant put to hauling field guns instead.

cells.name: Guinea Fowl
cells.cue: Loud, spotted yard bird kept as a living alarm for anything approaching at night.

cells.name: Quail
cells.cue: Small ground bird kept caged near the wire, bursts upward at the first tripped wire.

cells.name: Rooster
cells.cue: Crows on a handler's cue to mask a work party's noise at first light.

cells.name: Broody Hen
cells.cue: Sits tight on her clutch through shelling, barely flinching at the nearest impact.

cells.name: Kept Ornamental Swan
cells.cue: A parade-ground pond bird, hissing and preened, kept for the officers' show of normalcy.

cells.name: Caged Parakeet
cells.cue: Small bright cage-bird kept for morale, mimics the whistle-signal better than most soldiers.

cells.name: Guinea Pig
cells.cue: Small kept rodent, calm-tempered mascot passed hand to hand down the line.

cells.name: Hedgehog
cells.cue: Rolled tight at the first loud noise, kept in camp to clear the vermin the cats miss.

cells.name: Mongoose
cells.cue: Quick, low-slung ratter kept where the local rat population outpaces the cats.

cells.name: Civet
cells.cue: Nocturnal, musk-scented kept animal, prized (and traded) for the scent itself.

cells.name: Trained Raven
cells.cue: Taught to fetch bright objects for a camp entertainer's act, still does the trick unprompted.

cells.name: Barn Swallow
cells.cue: Nests under the eaves of whatever's still standing, unbothered by the noise below.

cells.name: Tame Polecat
cells.cue: Kept on a long leash for ratting the grain stores, bad-tempered and effective.

cells.name: Kept Honeybee Hive
cells.cue: A working hive kept for wax and the little sugar it still yields.

cells.name: Farmed Snail
cells.cue: Kept in a slatted crate as an emergency ration, glacially unbothered by anything.

cells.name: Kept Cochineal Beetle Brood
cells.cue: Crushed for the red dye that marks maps, bandages, and rank alike.

cells.name: Farmed Medicinal Leech Jar
cells.cue: A field medic's jar of them, kept fed and ready for the next wound.

cells.name: Wild animal — Territory wolf — holds a stretch of ground and knows every crossing of it
Wild animal — A single deer from the herd — moves with the herd, reads the wind before the ranger does
Wild animal — Watcher-hawk — sees the whole valley from height and forgets nothing it circled
Wild animal — River otter — knows the water's moods better than any map
Wild animal — Burrowing badger — knows what the earth carries underneath
Wild animal — Ambush lynx — solitary, patient, and the reason the trail went quiet
Wild animal — A single vulture from the carrion flock — first to know when something has died nearby
Wild animal — A single goose from the migrant flock — passes through and carries news of where it's been
Wild animal — Old solitary boar — scarred, wary, and gives ground to no one
Wild animal — Half-wild fringe fox — drawn to the edge of camps, curious and never quite trusting
Wild animal — The realm-beast (a battlefield crow, thick in numbers where the fighting was worst)
Wild animal — The elder of the wood — the beast every other animal on the node defers to
Wild animal — A single elk — grazes the tree line at dawn, gone before full light
Wild animal — A lone timber-wolf pup — not yet part of any pack, still learning to hunt
Wild animal — A red fox kit — curious, unafraid, too young to know better
Wild animal — A great owl — silent wingbeats, watches more than it hunts
Wild animal — A wild boar sow — tusks lowered, protective of ground she doesn't even own yet
Wild animal — A mountain goat — sure-footed on a ledge no predator bothers to follow
Wild animal — A black bear — foraging, unbothered, dangerous only if pressed
Wild animal — A heron — stalks the shallows on legs too thin to look that patient
Wild animal — A wild turkey tom — displaying, loud, oblivious to anything hunting it
Wild animal — A bull elk — antlers full-grown, the season's rut making it reckless
Wild animal — A badger — low, broad, digging with total disregard for anything nearby
Wild animal — A peregrine falcon — stooping mid-hunt, faster than anything else in the sky
Wild animal — A lynx kitten — spotted coat, play-stalking something that isn't there yet
Ptarmigan
cells.cue: Molts stark white for the season, near-invisible against frost and drifted ash.

cells.name: Color-Shifting Tree Frog
cells.cue: Skin shifts tone mid-perch to match whatever bark or char it's gripping.

cells.name: Stick-Mimic Insect
cells.cue: Body a dead ringer for a snapped twig, motionless on a shattered branch.

cells.name: Leaf-Mimic Insect
cells.cue: Wings veined and browned to match the dead leaves scattered around it.

cells.name: Bark-Pattern Moth
cells.cue: Wings flattened and patterned to vanish against scorched bark.

cells.name: Opossum
cells.cue: Drops and plays dead on cue, the oldest trick in the wild's own repertoire.

cells.name: Broken-Wing Plover
cells.cue: Fakes a crippled wing to drag a threat away from its ground nest.

cells.name: Nightjar
cells.cue: Plumage matches leaf-litter so exactly it's stepped on before it's seen.

cells.name: Woodcock
cells.cue: Freezes bill-down in dead brush, invisible until it explodes into flight.

cells.name: Ermine
cells.cue: Coat flips stark white with the season, a natural camouflage switch.

cells.name: Arctic Hare
cells.cue: Coat pales with the season, bounding low across churned, frost-white ground.

cells.name: Praying Mantis
cells.cue: Poised like a broken twig, motionless, until the strike.

cells.name: Bower-Building Songbird
cells.cue: Decorates its nest with scavenged shell-casings and bright shrapnel like stage-dressing.

cells.name: Crater-Nesting Swift
cells.cue: Wheels and roosts inside a blasted crater's lip, gone at first light.

cells.name: Shrapnel-Gleaming Magpie
cells.cue: Can't resist bright metal scraps off the field, nest glittering with them.

cells.name: Cordite-Drawn Midge Swarm
cells.cue: Thickens around any lit flare, easily mistaken for drifting smoke.

cells.name: Camouflage-Coated Weasel
cells.cue: Dun-and-shadow coat all season, moves like a thrown shadow through the grass.

cells.name: Distraction-Calling Grouse
cells.cue: Drums and flushes loud on purpose to pull attention off its brood.

cells.name: Debris-Burrowing Vole
cells.cue: Tunnels beneath collapsed earthworks, invisible until the ground itself moves.

cells.name: Flare-Startled Corncrake
cells.cue: A secretive ground bird that only breaks cover when a flare goes up.

cells.name: Ash-Dusted Jackal
cells.cue: Coat pale with drifting ash, barely a shape against the wasted ground.

cells.name: Wire-Perching Shrike
cells.cue: Impales its catch on barbed wire the same as it would thorns.

cells.name: Mimic Cuckoo
cells.cue: Lays in another bird's nest and vanishes before the switch is ever noticed.

cells.name: Frost-Pale Lemming
cells.cue: Coat pales to match frost-rimed ground, burrows between the artillery's lulls.

cells.name: Motionless Mudflat Toad
cells.cue: Skin the exact color of churned mud, holds dead still through the barrage's rumble.

Dungeon animal — Blind cave rat — pale, sightless, thrives in total dark, first sign something's been dug through
Dungeon animal — Tunnel bat colony straggler — a single bat that never rejoined the swarm, clings alone near a cracked vent
Dungeon animal — Half-tamed thing — comes to a lantern's light, never a hand, feeds on what the dungeon leaves behind
Dungeon animal — Lost hunting hound — a noble's dog that wandered too far in and never found the way back out
Dungeon animal — Cave-adapted spider — pale, eyeless, spins webs across passages nobody's walked in years
Dungeon animal — Wrong-place goat — a farm animal that fell through a sinkhole and somehow survived down here
Dungeon animal — Glow-moss grazer — a small rodent whose fur has picked up a faint luminescence from what it eats
Dungeon animal — Echo-startled bird — a single bird trapped in the upper galleries, flies at every footstep
Dungeon animal — Scarred guard-dog gone feral — once trained to patrol these halls, now answers to no one
Dungeon animal — Blind salamander — pale, slow, the kind of thing that shouldn't have a reason to be this deep
Dungeon animal — Starving stray — a cat or dog that followed someone in and got left behind
Dungeon animal — Unnervingly large lone rat — alone, watching, doesn't scatter like the others
Dungeon animal — Tunnel-adapted snake — pale-scaled, sluggish in the cold, strikes only when cornered
Dungeon animal — Chained beast, escaped its post — a working animal that slipped its old restraint, still wears the collar
Dungeon animal — Nest-robbing crow — one bird that's learned the dungeon's side passages better than most explorers
Dungeon animal — Deep-well fish, stranded — flopping in a puddle far from any real water source
Dungeon animal — Sole survivor packhorse — the last of a caravan's animals, malnourished, still saddled
Dungeon animal — Cave cricket, oversized — chirping alone in the dark, first warning of the swarm nearby
Dungeon animal — Feral falconry bird — a hawk that escaped its jesses generations ago, now hunts the tunnels' vermin
Dungeon animal — Wrongly-still lizard — motionless so long it's mistaken for a carving, until it isn't
Dungeon animal — Abandoned mine canary — a small bird in a rusted cage, somehow still alive, still singing
Dungeon animal — Tunnel-blind mole — huge clawed forepaws, displaces more earth than it should be able to

Cave Glowworm
cells.cue: Strung along the tunnel roof like dim stage-lights nobody installed.

cells.name: Cave Silverfish
cells.cue: Slips through stacked ammunition crates and old paper stores, first sign of long neglect.

cells.name: Cave Millipede
cells.cue: Pale, segmented, ripples along the tunnel wall untouched by the light.

cells.name: Blind Cave Shrimp
cells.cue: Colorless, eyeless, drifts in flooded sump water nobody's checked in months.

cells.name: Displaced Circus Monkey
cells.cue: Trained to tumble and salute, still performs the trick alone in the dark.

cells.name: Escaped Mimic Starling
cells.cue: Trained for a camp entertainer's act, still parrots a laugh from nowhere nearby.

cells.name: Ghost-Pale Cave Weevil
cells.cue: Colorless, wingless, scuttles over unexploded ordnance without setting it off.

cells.name: Sump-Dwelling Flatworm
cells.cue: Thrives in the flooded gallery water nobody's tested since the mine went in.

cells.name: Tallow-Candle Grub
cells.cue: Burrows into stored candle-stubs, the sappers' unwelcome sign the stores went unchecked.

cells.name: Deep-Shaft Centipede
cells.cue: Pale, many-legged, ambushes anything smaller that stumbles into the collapsed gallery.

cells.name: Echo-Blind Cave Cockroach
cells.cue: Swarms briefly whenever a charge goes off nearby, then vanishes into the rubble.

cells.name: Flare-Answering Firefly Swarm
cells.cue: Winged, drawn to true signal flares, mistaken twice now for enemy semaphore.

cells.name: Sunken Duckboard Eel
cells.cue: Writhes in standing water beneath rotted duckboards, blind and the color of drowned wood.

cells.name: Displaced Trained Jackdaw
cells.cue: Learned to fetch bright objects for a camp act, now hoards shell-casings in a dead-end gallery.

cells.name: Chalk-Pale Cave Woodlouse
cells.cue: Rolls tight at the smallest vibration, the tunnel's most reliable tremor-gauge.

cells.name: Trapped Performing Seal
cells.cue: Barks in the flooded lower gallery, still angling for a fish that isn't coming.

cells.name: Runaway Sideshow Scorpion
cells.cue: Escaped a traveling show's box, glows faint violet under any stray UV light down here.

cells.name: Ash-Pale Cave Slug
cells.cue: Glistens faintly in lantern light, slow enough to pass for old wax drippings.

cells.name: Blind Cave Gecko
cells.cue: Clings motionless to the tunnel roof, translucent skin lit faint violet by leftover flare-glow.

cells.name: Cave-Adapted Harvestman

cells.name: Lost Regimental Mascot Tortoise
cells.cue: Carried as a slow-motion good-luck charm, forgotten down here years back, still alive.

cells.name: Phosphor-Dusted Springtail Swarm
cells.cue: Lifts off any disturbed patch of mold, faint green-gold in lantern light.

cells.name: Understudy Finch, Caged
cells.cue: Kept as a spare for the mine canary, never once tested, feathers dulled from disuse.

cells.name: A Once-Trained Animal, Unremarkable Now
cells.cue: Some camp performer's old act, species hardly matters down here; its being lost IS the signal.

cells.name: Blind Cave Skink
cells.cue: Pale-scaled, eyeless, suns itself uselessly under a cracked shaft's sliver of light.
